key_concepts: Friction is a force that opposes motion and acts opposite to the direction of motion
Rough surfaces produce more friction than smooth surfaces
Objects slow down more quickly on rough surfaces
Static, sliding, rolling, and fluid friction are types of friction
Static friction acts opposite an applied force on a stationary object
Fluid friction acts on objects moving through water or air
Rolling friction occurs with wheels, strollers, pushcarts, and roller skates
Sliding friction occurs when surfaces slide past each other
Gravity pulls objects toward Earth's center
Gravitational pull is weaker on the moon than on Earth
Without air resistance, objects dropped from the same height hit the ground at the same ti
Free fall is falling without air resistance; the sun's gravity keeps planets in orbit
